::: {.callout-note appearance="simple" icon=false}

1. Methods come in two families: regression methods pick terms from a library that you propose, and symbolic regression builds the terms too.

2. SINDy and global modelling are regression methods. SINDy returns one sparse model; global modelling returns many candidates and checks each one by simulation.

3. A discovered equation is a hypothesis, not proof of a mechanism.

:::

Today I learned about equation discovery from Quynh Anh's talk ([her code](https://github.com/quingzz/equation_discovery_ppt)). You start with time series from a system, stored as a data matrix $X$ with one row per time point and one column per variable. You want the differential equations that generated them: a system $dX/dt = F(X)$.

Why bother? Differential equations can capture strongly nonlinear dynamics, and you can read every term in them. So equation discovery gives an interpretable model built from data, and it may point to mechanisms we did not know about.

## The test case: the Lorenz system

To test a method, it helps to use a system whose equations we already know, so we can check the answer. The talk used the Lorenz system (Lorenz 1963):

$$
\begin{aligned}
\frac{dx}{dt} &= \sigma (y - x) \\
\frac{dy}{dt} &= x (\rho - z) - y \\
\frac{dz}{dt} &= x y - \beta z
\end{aligned}
$$

with $\sigma = 10$, $\rho = 28$, $\beta = 8/3$ and the starting point $(10, 10, 10)$. Multiplied out, the right-hand sides are $10y - 10x$, $28x - xz - y$ and $xy - 2.667z$, so there are 7 terms. The problem is this: given only the three time series below, can a method find these 7 terms and their values?

```{ojs}
import {
  simulateLorenz, prepareData, polyTerms, termLabel, evalTerms, gramSystem, lsSubset, rss,
  stlsq, backwardElimination, combineLadders, simulatePoly, dataStats,
  makeOverlapScorer, runCandidate, OUTCOMES, lorenzTrueCoefs, thin, extent
} from "./equation-discovery.js"
import { tokens, watchTheme, motion, makeCard, button, segmented, legend, watchWidth } from "../../js/viz.js"
```

```{ojs}
VARS = ["x", "y", "z"]
EQS = ["dx/dt", "dy/dt", "dz/dt"]
DOTS = ["ẋ", "ẏ", "ż"]
lorenz = simulateLorenz({ dt: 0.01, tEnd: 100, substeps: 10 })
base = prepareData(lorenz.t, lorenz.X, { win: 9, order: 4 })
// the stretch of data drawn in the column figures: 4 time units, every second point
WIN = d3.range(996, 1397, 2)
// one library for both methods: all polynomials up to degree 2, with the constant
lib = {
  const terms = polyTerms(3, 2, true);
  const cols = evalTerms(terms, base.X);
  const sys = gramSystem(cols, base.dX);
  const all = terms.map((_, i) => i);
  return {
    terms, cols, sys,
    labels: terms.map((t) => termLabel(t)),
    factors: terms.map((t) => t.flatMap((p, j) => Array(p).fill(j))),
    truth: lorenzTrueCoefs(terms),
    lsCoef: sys.eqs.map((q) => lsSubset(sys.G, q.b, all)),
    ladders: sys.eqs.map((q) => backwardElimination(sys.G, q.b, q.yy))
  };
}
gp = ({ terms: lib.terms, labels: lib.labels, truth: lib.truth, ladders: lib.ladders, models: combineLadders(lib.ladders, 6, 11) })
// The GPoM candidates are simulated only when the last figure needs them, a few at a time,
// so the page never freezes. Each run is kept here and reused.
gpCache = ({ stats: dataStats(base.X), scorer: makeOverlapScorer(base.X, 0, 2), runs: new Map() })
```

```{ojs}
// colours come from the site theme; this cell runs again when the reader switches light or dark,
// and every figure that uses them redraws
VIZ = Generators.observe((notify) => watchTheme(() => notify(tokens())))
// The colour rule of this post: a colour means a variable and its equation (x and dx/dt,
// y and dy/dt, z and dz/dt: the first three group colours, checked for colour-blind
// separation in both modes). A path in the plane of x and z is drawn in ink, and data shown
// for comparison in grey.
EQC = VIZ.cat.slice(0, 3)
// a weight, written as in the slides: two decimals, "≈0" when it is tiny but not zero,
// and "0" when its term has been removed
function fmtW(c) {
  if (c === 0) return "0";
  const a = Math.abs(c);
  return a < 0.005 ? "≈0" : (c < 0 ? "−" : "") + a.toFixed(2);
}
function fmtLambda(l) {
  return String(Number(l.toPrecision(2)));
}
function fmtPct(r) {
  const p = 100 * r;
  return (p < 1 ? p.toFixed(2) : p < 10 ? p.toFixed(1) : p.toFixed(0)) + "%";
}
function termName(i) {
  return lib.labels[i] === "1" ? "the constant" : lib.labels[i];
}
function sameTerms(coef, truth) {
  return Array.from(coef).every((c, i) => (c !== 0) === (truth[i] !== 0));
}
// The right-hand side of an equation as text, for example "−9.998 x + 9.998 y". Weights are
// written with `digits` significant digits, or with `fixed` decimals as in the rows of weights.
// Weights smaller than `cut` are counted, not written.
function eqRhs(coef, { cut = 0, digits = 4, fixed = null } = {}) {
  const parts = [];
  let nTiny = 0;
  Array.from(coef).forEach((c, i) => {
    if (c === 0) return;
    if (Math.abs(c) < cut) return nTiny++;
    const num = fixed === null ? String(Number(Math.abs(c).toPrecision(digits))) : Math.abs(c).toFixed(fixed);
    const name = lib.labels[i] === "1" ? "" : lib.labels[i];
    const body = name && num === "1" ? name : name ? `${num} ${name}` : num;
    parts.push(parts.length ? ` ${c < 0 ? "−" : "+"} ${body}` : `${c < 0 ? "−" : ""}${body}`);
  });
  return { text: parts.join("") || "0", tiny: nTiny ? ` + ${nTiny} tiny ${nTiny === 1 ? "term" : "terms"}` : "" };
}
// The name of an equation after a dot in its colour
function eqName(j) {
  return html`<span style="display:inline-flex;align-items:baseline;gap:0.5rem;white-space:nowrap;font-weight:500;color:var(--viz-ink)">
    <span style="flex:none;width:0.58rem;height:0.58rem;border-radius:50%;background:${EQC[j]};transform:translateY(-0.06em)"></span>${EQS[j]} =</span>`;
}
// One equation as a line of text. coef: its 10 weights, or null when the equation is not found yet.
function eqLine(j, coef, options = {}) {
  const r = coef ? eqRhs(coef, options) : { text: "?", tiny: "" };
  return html`<div style="display:flex;align-items:baseline;gap:0.45rem;padding:2px 0;font-variant-numeric:tabular-nums">${eqName(j)}
    <span style="color:var(${coef ? "--viz-ink" : "--viz-muted"})">${r.text}<span style="color:var(--viz-muted)">${r.tiny}</span></span></div>`;
}
// A small marker above a card's title: the method, and which of its four steps the figure shows.
function eyebrow(card, method) {
  const bars = d3.range(4).map(() => html`<span style="width:18px;height:2px;border-radius:1px"></span>`);
  const text = html`<span></span>`;
  card.root.insertBefore(
    html`<div style="display:flex;align-items:center;gap:10px;margin:0 0 6px;font-size:var(--fs-label);font-weight:500;color:var(--viz-muted)">
      <span style="display:inline-flex;gap:3px" aria-hidden="true">${bars}</span>${text}</div>`,
    card.root.firstChild
  );
  function set(k, label) {
    bars.forEach((b, i) => (b.style.background = `var(${i === k ? "--viz-ink" : "--viz-rule"})`));
    text.textContent = `${method}, step ${k + 1} of 4: ${label}`;
    return api;
  }
  const api = { set };
  return api;
}
// The body of a card as a chart with a column of text: beside it on a wide card, under it on a narrow one.
function split(body, width, sideW = 290) {
  const wide = width >= 760;
  const cw = wide ? width - sideW - 26 : width;
  const sw = wide ? sideW : width;
  const chart = html`<div class="viz-col" style="width:${cw}px"></div>`;
  const side = html`<div class="viz-side" style="width:${sw}px"></div>`;
  body.innerHTML = "";
  body.append(chart, side);
  return { chart, side, cw, sw, wide };
}
// Back and Next for a figure that runs in steps. The arrow keys work when the card has focus,
// and a sideways swipe on `swipe` (a phone or a tablet) goes to the next or the previous step.
// go(k, animate) draws step k; count() is the number of steps.
function stepper({ count, go, label = null, root = null, swipe = null }) {
  let k = 0;
  const counter = html`<span class="viz-readout" aria-live="polite"></span>`;
  const back = button("◀ Back", () => to(k - 1));
  const next = button("Next ▶", () => to(k >= count() - 1 ? 0 : k + 1));
  function refresh() {
    const n = count();
    back.disabled = k === 0;
    next.textContent = k >= n - 1 ? "Start again" : "Next ▶";
    counter.textContent = label ? label(k) : `${k + 1} of ${n}`;
  }
  function to(j, animate = true) {
    k = Math.max(0, Math.min(count() - 1, j));
    go(k, animate);
    refresh();
  }
  const onKey = (ev) => {
    if (ev.target.closest("input, select, textarea")) return;
    if (ev.key === "ArrowRight" && k < count() - 1) { ev.preventDefault(); to(k + 1); }
    else if (ev.key === "ArrowLeft" && k > 0) { ev.preventDefault(); to(k - 1); }
  };
  if (root) root.addEventListener("keydown", onKey);
  if (swipe) {
    // pan-y: the page still scrolls up and down; a sideways move is left to the figure
    swipe.style.touchAction = "pan-y";
    let x0 = null, y0 = 0;
    swipe.addEventListener("pointerdown", (ev) => { if (ev.pointerType !== "mouse") { x0 = ev.clientX; y0 = ev.clientY; } });
    swipe.addEventListener("pointercancel", () => { x0 = null; });
    swipe.addEventListener("pointerup", (ev) => {
      if (x0 === null) return;
      const dx = ev.clientX - x0, dy = ev.clientY - y0;
      x0 = null;
      if (Math.abs(dx) > 48 && Math.abs(dx) > 1.5 * Math.abs(dy)) to(k + (dx < 0 ? 1 : -1));
    });
  }
  return { node: html`<div class="viz-btns">${back}${next}</div>`, counter, to, refresh, get k() { return k; } };
}
// The picture shared by three figures. On top: the derivative of one equation, with the weighted
// sum of the terms drawn over it. Under it: one row per candidate term, with its weight, its name
// and a small line over 4 time units. On the right (optional): Ξ as a grid of dots, one column per
// equation. set(state) draws a state:
//   mode "library": the terms only, each line scaled to its own range
//   mode "unknown": the derivative appears and the weights are "?"
//   mode "fit":     the weights in `coef`; each line is weight × term, all on one scale. A term
//                   that adds almost nothing is a flat line, and its row shrinks, so the terms
//                   that carry the equation get the room.
//   off: the removed terms, below: the terms to outline, xi: a state for each dot ("u", "on", "off")
function termRows(width, { dots = true } = {}) {
  const n = lib.labels.length, m = WIN.length, idx = d3.range(m);
  const narrow = width < 520;
  const wW = narrow ? 50 : 60;               // right edge of the weights
  const xName = wW + 24;                     // left edge of the names
  const xS0 = xName + (narrow ? 30 : 36);    // the lines run from here ...
  const pitch = narrow ? 15 : 18;
  const xS1 = width - (dots ? 14 + 3 * pitch : 4);   // ... to here
  const xDot = (j) => xS1 + 12 + pitch / 2 + j * pitch;
  const tgtH = narrow ? 70 : 84, top = 26, thin = 17;
  const rowsH = n * (narrow ? 26 : 28);
  const yT = top + tgtH / 2, yR0 = top + tgtH + 44, yLib = 34;
  const H = yR0 + rowsH + 4;
  const xs = d3.scaleLinear().domain([0, m - 1]).range([xS0, xS1]);
  const amp = (f) => { let a = 0; for (let i = 0; i < m; i++) a = Math.max(a, Math.abs(f(i))); return a || 1; };
  const termAmp = lib.cols.map((c) => amp((i) => c[WIN[i]]));
  const lineOf = (f) => d3.line().x((i) => xs(i)).y((i) => f(i))(idx);
  const areaOf = (f) => d3.area().x((i) => xs(i)).y0(0).y1((i) => f(i))(idx);
  const svg = d3.create("svg").attr("class", "viz-svg").attr("width", width).attr("height", H).attr("role", "img");
  const small = (sel) => sel.attr("class", "viz-muted").style("font-size", "12px");
  // the derivative, and the sum of the rows over it
  const gT = svg.append("g");
  const clip = DOM.uid("clip");
  gT.append("clipPath").attr("id", clip.id).append("rect").attr("x", xS0).attr("y", top - 3).attr("width", xS1 - xS0).attr("height", tgtH + 6);
  gT.append("line").attr("x1", xS0).attr("x2", xS1).attr("y1", yT).attr("y2", yT).attr("stroke", VIZ.rule);
  const target = gT.append("path").attr("fill", "none").attr("stroke-width", 2).attr("stroke-linejoin", "round").attr("clip-path", clip);
  const fit = gT.append("path").attr("fill", "none").attr("stroke", VIZ.ink).attr("stroke-width", 1.1).attr("stroke-dasharray", "4,3").attr("clip-path", clip);
  const tName = gT.append("text").attr("x", xS0 - 10).attr("y", yT).attr("dy", "0.35em").attr("text-anchor", "end").attr("font-weight", 600).style("font-size", "14px");
  const lx = narrow ? 0 : xS0;
  const lgData = gT.append("g").attr("transform", `translate(${lx},9)`);
  const lgSwatch = lgData.append("line").attr("x2", 16).attr("stroke-width", 2);
  small(lgData.append("text").attr("x", 22).attr("dy", "0.35em")).text("from the data");
  const lgFit = gT.append("g").attr("transform", `translate(${lx + 116},9)`);
  lgFit.append("line").attr("x2", 16).attr("stroke", VIZ.ink).attr("stroke-width", 1.1).attr("stroke-dasharray", "4,3");
  const lgFitText = small(lgFit.append("text").attr("x", 22).attr("dy", "0.35em"));
  // headings of the rows (they move with the rows)
  const gH = svg.append("g");
  const hWeight = small(gH.append("text").attr("x", wW).attr("y", -11).attr("text-anchor", "end")).text("weight");
  if (!narrow) small(gH.append("text").attr("x", xName).attr("y", -11)).text("term");
  const hLine = small(gH.append("text").attr("x", xS0).attr("y", -11));
  // Ξ: one column of dots per equation, under its name and a bar in its colour
  const gXi = svg.append("g").attr("transform", `translate(0,${yR0})`);
  let plate = null;
  if (dots) {
    plate = gXi.append("rect").attr("y", -42).attr("width", pitch).attr("height", rowsH + 46).attr("rx", 5).attr("fill", VIZ.wash);
    small(gXi.append("text").attr("x", xDot(1)).attr("y", -47).attr("text-anchor", "middle")).text("Ξ");
    DOTS.forEach((d, j) => {
      gXi.append("text").attr("x", xDot(j)).attr("y", -19).attr("text-anchor", "middle").attr("font-weight", 500).style("font-size", "12.5px").text(d);
      gXi.append("rect").attr("x", xDot(j) - 5).attr("y", -14).attr("width", 10).attr("height", 2.5).attr("rx", 1.25).attr("fill", EQC[j]);
    });
  }
  // the rows: each group sits on the centre line of its row
  const row = svg.append("g").selectAll("g").data(d3.range(n)).join("g");
  row.append("line").attr("x1", xS0).attr("x2", xS1).attr("stroke", VIZ.rule);
  const area = row.append("path").attr("stroke", "none").attr("fill-opacity", 0.13);
  const line = row.append("path").attr("fill", "none").attr("stroke-width", 1.4).attr("stroke-linejoin", "round");
  const box = row.append("rect").attr("x", wW - 44).attr("y", -8.5).attr("width", 49).attr("height", 17).attr("rx", 4.5)
    .attr("fill", "none").attr("stroke", VIZ.ink).attr("stroke-width", 1).attr("opacity", 0);
  const wt = row.append("text").attr("x", wW).attr("dy", "0.35em").attr("text-anchor", "end").style("font-size", "13.5px");
  const mul = small(row.append("text").attr("x", wW + 13).attr("dy", "0.35em").attr("text-anchor", "middle")).text("×");
  const nm = row.append("text").attr("x", xName).attr("dy", "0.35em").attr("font-weight", 500).style("font-size", "13.5px").text((k) => lib.labels[k]);
  const dot = dots ? row.selectAll("circle").data((k) => [0, 1, 2].map((j) => ({ k, j }))).join("circle").attr("cx", (d) => xDot(d.j)).attr("r", 0) : null;
  let drawn = false;
  function set(s, animate = true) {
    const e = s.e, dur = motion(animate && drawn ? 500 : 0);
    const isLib = s.mode === "library", isFit = s.mode === "fit";
    const off = new Set(s.off || []), below = new Set(s.below || []);
    const coef = s.coef || [];
    const go = (sel) => (dur ? sel.interrupt().transition().duration(dur) : sel.interrupt());
    svg.attr("aria-label", isLib ? "The 10 candidate terms over 4 time units" : `${EQS[e]} as a weighted sum of the 10 candidate terms`);
    // the derivative and the sum
    const tv = (i) => base.dX[e][WIN[i]];
    const aT = amp(tv);
    const yOf = (v) => yT - (v / aT) * (tgtH / 2 - 6);
    go(gT).attr("opacity", isLib ? 0 : 1);
    tName.text(EQS[e]);
    target.attr("stroke", EQC[e]).attr("d", lineOf((i) => yOf(tv(i))));
    lgSwatch.attr("stroke", EQC[e]);
    lgFit.attr("opacity", isFit ? 1 : 0);
    fit.interrupt().attr("opacity", isFit ? 1 : 0);
    if (isFit) {
      const sum = (i) => { let v = 0; for (let k = 0; k < n; k++) if (!off.has(k) && coef[k]) v += coef[k] * lib.cols[k][WIN[i]]; return v; };
      const d = lineOf((i) => yOf(sum(i)));
      (fit.attr("d") ? go(fit) : fit).attr("d", d);
      lgFitText.text(`sum of the rows${s.err == null ? "" : narrow ? `, error ${fmtPct(s.err)}` : ` (fit error ${fmtPct(s.err)})`}`);
    }
    // how tall each row is: in a fit, a term that adds under 2% of the largest one gets a thin row
    const size = (k) => (isFit && !off.has(k) ? Math.abs(coef[k] || 0) * termAmp[k] : 0);
    const cAmp = d3.max(d3.range(n), size) || 1;
    const big = d3.range(n).map((k) => isFit && size(k) >= 0.02 * cAmp);
    const nBig = big.filter(Boolean).length;
    const y0 = isLib ? yLib : yR0, total = isLib ? H - yLib - 4 : rowsH;
    const tall = Math.min(88, (total - (n - nBig) * thin) / Math.max(1, nBig));
    const h = d3.range(n).map((k) => (!isFit || nBig === 0 ? total / n : big[k] ? tall : thin));
    const yc = [];
    h.reduce((acc, hk, k) => ((yc[k] = acc + hk / 2), acc + hk), y0);
    const unit = isFit ? (Math.max(tall, thin) / 2 - 5) / cAmp : 0;   // pixels per unit of weight × term
    go(gH).attr("transform", `translate(0,${y0})`);
    hWeight.attr("opacity", isLib ? 0 : 1);
    hLine.text(isFit ? "weight × term over 4 time units" : narrow ? "the term over 4 time units" : "its values over 4 time units");
    go(row).attr("transform", (k) => `translate(0,${yc[k]})`);
    line.each(function (k) {
      const col = lib.cols[k], halfLib = h[k] / 2 - 4;
      const f = !isFit ? (i) => (-col[WIN[i]] / termAmp[k]) * halfLib : off.has(k) ? () => 0 : (i) => -coef[k] * col[WIN[i]] * unit;
      const el = d3.select(this), ar = d3.select(area.nodes()[k]);
      el.attr("stroke", isFit ? (off.has(k) ? VIZ.faint : EQC[e]) : k >= 1 && k <= 3 ? EQC[k - 1] : VIZ.text);
      ar.attr("fill", isFit && !off.has(k) ? EQC[e] : "none");
      (el.attr("d") ? go(el) : el).attr("d", lineOf(f));
      (ar.attr("d") ? go(ar) : ar).attr("d", areaOf(f));
    });
    const label = (k) => (isLib ? "" : !isFit ? "?" : off.has(k) ? "0" : fmtW(coef[k]));
    wt.text(label)
      .attr("font-weight", (k) => (isFit && !off.has(k) && label(k) !== "≈0" ? 500 : 400))
      .style("fill", (k) => (!isFit || off.has(k) ? VIZ.muted : label(k) === "≈0" ? VIZ.text : VIZ.ink));
    mul.attr("opacity", isLib ? 0 : 1);
    nm.style("fill", (k) => (isFit && off.has(k) ? VIZ.muted : VIZ.ink));
    go(box).attr("opacity", (k) => (isFit && below.has(k) ? 1 : 0));
    // Ξ
    if (dots) {
      go(gXi).attr("opacity", isLib ? 0 : 1);
      plate.attr("x", xDot(e) - pitch / 2);
      dot.each(function (d) {
        const v = isLib || !s.xi ? null : s.xi[d.j][d.k];
        go(d3.select(this).attr("fill", v === "on" ? EQC[d.j] : v === "off" ? VIZ.grey : "none").attr("stroke", v === "u" ? VIZ.grey : "none"))
          .attr("r", v === "on" ? 4.2 : v === "u" ? 3.4 : v === "off" ? 1.3 : 0);
      });
    }
    drawn = true;
  }
  return { node: svg.node(), set, height: H };
}
```

```{ojs}
{
  const T = 30, TAIL = 2.5;
  const idx = thin(Math.round(T / 0.01) + 1, 1500);
  const tt = idx.map((i) => lorenz.t[i]);
  const XX = VARS.map((_, j) => idx.map((i) => lorenz.X[j][i]));
  const whole = thin(lorenz.t.length, 4000).map((i) => [lorenz.X[0][i], lorenz.X[2][i]]);
  const step = tt[1] - tt[0];
  let tNow = 8, frame = null, draw = () => {};
  const { root, toolbar, body } = makeCard(
    "The data",
    "One run of the Lorenz system: three time series, and the same run in the plane of x and z. Press Play, or drag across the chart."
  );
  const slider = html`<input type="range" class="viz-range" min="0" max="${T}" step="0.01" aria-label="Time">`;
  slider.value = tNow;
  const readout = html`<span class="viz-readout"></span>`;
  const stop = () => {
    if (frame) cancelAnimationFrame(frame);
    frame = null;
    play.textContent = "▶ Play";
  };
  const play = button("▶ Play", () => {
    if (frame) return stop();
    if (tNow >= T - 0.01) tNow = 0;
    play.textContent = "❚❚ Pause";
    const tick = () => {
      tNow = Math.min(T, tNow + 0.04);
      slider.value = tNow;
      draw();
      if (tNow < T) frame = requestAnimationFrame(tick);
      else stop();
    };
    frame = requestAnimationFrame(tick);
  });
  slider.oninput = () => {
    stop();
    tNow = +slider.value;
    draw();
  };
  toolbar.append(play, slider, readout);
  invalidation.then(stop);
  watchWidth(root, (w) => {
    body.innerHTML = "";
    const wide = w >= 680;
    const wTs = wide ? Math.floor((w - 26) * 0.6) : w;
    const wPh = wide ? w - 26 - wTs : Math.min(w, 400);
    const mL = 34, hP = 84, gap = 10, hAxis = 26;
    const hTs = 3 * hP + 2 * gap + hAxis;
    // the three time series: one panel each, one time axis under the last
    const x = d3.scaleLinear().domain([0, T]).range([mL, wTs - 6]);
    const ts = d3.create("svg").attr("class", "viz-svg").attr("width", wTs).attr("height", hTs).style("touch-action", "pan-y").style("cursor", "ew-resize")
      .attr("role", "img").attr("aria-label", "x, y and z of the Lorenz system over 30 time units");
    const cursor = ts.append("line").attr("y1", 0).attr("y2", hTs - hAxis).attr("stroke", VIZ.grey).attr("stroke-width", 1);
    const marks = VARS.map((v, j) => {
      const y0 = j * (hP + gap);
      const y = d3.scaleLinear().domain(extent(lorenz.X[j])).range([y0 + hP - 4, y0 + 6]);
      const [lo, hi] = y.domain();
      // only the two ends of the range are labelled, so the lines carry the picture
      for (const v of [lo, hi]) {
        ts.append("text").attr("x", mL - 6).attr("y", y(v)).attr("dy", "0.35em").attr("text-anchor", "end").attr("class", "viz-muted").style("font-size", "11px").text(Math.round(v));
      }
      if (lo < 0) ts.append("line").attr("x1", mL).attr("x2", wTs - 6).attr("y1", y(0)).attr("y2", y(0)).attr("stroke", VIZ.rule);
      ts.append("path").attr("d", d3.line().x((_, i) => x(tt[i])).y((d) => y(d))(XX[j])).attr("fill", "none").attr("stroke", EQC[j]).attr("stroke-width", 1.5).attr("stroke-linejoin", "round");
      ts.append("text").attr("x", mL - 6).attr("y", y0 + hP / 2).attr("dy", "0.35em").attr("text-anchor", "end").attr("font-weight", 600).style("font-size", "14px").text(v);
      const dot = ts.append("circle").attr("r", 4).attr("fill", EQC[j]).attr("stroke", VIZ.bg).attr("stroke-width", 2);
      return { y, dot };
    });
    ts.append("g").attr("transform", `translate(0,${hTs - hAxis})`).call(d3.axisBottom(x).ticks(wTs < 420 ? 4 : 6).tickSize(4).tickSizeOuter(0));
    ts.append("text").attr("x", wTs - 6).attr("y", hTs - 1).attr("text-anchor", "end").attr("class", "viz-muted").style("font-size", "12px").text("time");
    // dragging across the series moves the time (a sideways drag on a touch screen)
    const scrub = (ev) => {
      if (ev.type === "pointermove" && ev.pointerType === "mouse" && ev.buttons !== 1) return;
      // keep following the pointer when it leaves the chart during a drag
      if (ev.type === "pointerdown") { try { ts.node().setPointerCapture(ev.pointerId); } catch (_) {} }
      stop();
      tNow = Math.max(0, Math.min(T, x.invert(d3.pointer(ev, ts.node())[0])));
      slider.value = tNow;
      draw();
    };
    ts.on("pointerdown pointermove", scrub);
    // the same run in the plane of x and z
    const hPh = wide ? hTs : Math.round(wPh * 0.78);
    const ph = d3.create("svg").attr("class", "viz-svg").attr("width", wPh).attr("height", hPh)
      .attr("role", "img").attr("aria-label", "The same run in the plane of x and z");
    const xp = d3.scaleLinear().domain([-22, 22]).range([30, wPh - 6]);
    const zp = d3.scaleLinear().domain([0, 50]).range([hPh - hAxis, 8]);
    ph.append("g").attr("transform", `translate(0,${hPh - hAxis})`).call(d3.axisBottom(xp).ticks(5).tickSize(4).tickSizeOuter(0));
    ph.append("g").attr("transform", "translate(30,0)").call(d3.axisLeft(zp).ticks(5).tickSize(4).tickSizeOuter(0));
    ph.append("text").attr("x", wPh - 6).attr("y", hPh - 1).attr("text-anchor", "end").attr("font-weight", 600).style("font-size", "13px").text("x");
    ph.append("text").attr("x", 36).attr("y", 14).attr("font-weight", 600).style("font-size", "13px").text("z");
    ph.append("path").attr("d", d3.line().x((d) => xp(d[0])).y((d) => zp(d[1]))(whole)).attr("class", "viz-faint").attr("stroke-width", 0.8);
    const pts = tt.map((_, i) => [xp(XX[0][i]), zp(XX[2][i])]);
    // the run so far in thin ink, and its last 2.5 time units in full ink
    const past = ph.append("path").attr("fill", "none").attr("stroke", VIZ.ink).attr("stroke-width", 0.8).attr("stroke-opacity", 0.35).attr("stroke-linejoin", "round");
    const tail = ph.append("path").attr("fill", "none").attr("stroke", VIZ.ink).attr("stroke-width", 1.5).attr("stroke-linejoin", "round").attr("stroke-linecap", "round");
    const dot = ph.append("circle").attr("r", 4.5).attr("fill", VIZ.ink).attr("stroke", VIZ.bg).attr("stroke-width", 2);
    body.append(ts.node(), ph.node());
    draw = () => {
      const k = Math.min(tt.length - 1, Math.round(tNow / step));
      const k0 = Math.max(0, k - Math.round(TAIL / step));
      cursor.attr("x1", x(tNow)).attr("x2", x(tNow));
      marks.forEach((m, j) => m.dot.attr("cx", x(tNow)).attr("cy", m.y(XX[j][k])));
      past.attr("d", k0 > 0 ? d3.line()(pts.slice(0, k0 + 1)) : null);
      tail.attr("d", k > k0 ? d3.line()(pts.slice(k0, k + 1)) : null);
      dot.attr("cx", pts[k][0]).attr("cy", pts[k][1]);
      readout.textContent = `time ${tNow.toFixed(1)}`;
    };
    draw();
  }, invalidation);
  return root;
}
```
:::

## Two families of methods

The talk sorted the methods into two families. They differ in where the candidate terms come from: you propose them, or the algorithm builds them.

- Regression-based methods start from a library of candidate terms that you propose, such as $x$, $xz$ or $z^2$. A regression then selects the terms that stay and estimates their weights. SINDy and global modelling both work this way.
- Symbolic regression, listed in the slides under genetic algorithms, builds the terms from variables, numbers and operations such as $+$, $\times$ and $\sin$. In the version used by Schmidt and Lipson (2009), new equations are made by recombining and randomly changing earlier ones, and the ones that fit the data better are kept. No library is needed, but there are far more equations to search.

A 2023 review adds a third group that combines these ideas with neural networks (North, Wikle and Schliep 2023). Like the talk, this post sticks to regression.

## The regression recipe

A regression-based method treats each derivative as the outcome and the candidate terms as the predictors. The slides use three steps, and the figures add a fourth to check the result:

1. Compute the derivatives $dX/dt$ from the data.
2. Propose a library $\Theta(X)$ of candidate terms: here all 10 polynomials in $x$, $y$ and $z$ up to degree 2.
3. Fit $dX/dt \approx \Theta(X)\,\Xi$, where $\Xi$ holds one weight per term and equation.
4. Simulate the fitted system and compare it with the data.

::: {.viz-wide}
```{ojs}
{
  const t0 = base.t[WIN[0]], t1 = base.t[WIN[WIN.length - 1]];
  const STEPS = [
    { k: 0, label: "compute dX/dt", text: (q, v) => `<b>Step 1.</b> ${q} is the slope of ${v} at each moment. A Savitzky-Golay filter estimates it from a few neighbouring points. Drag across the chart to move the tangent line.` },
    { k: 1, label: "propose candidate terms", text: () => `<b>Step 2.</b> The library Θ(X) holds every term that an equation might use: here the 10 polynomials in x, y and z up to degree 2. Each one is computed from the data. For example, xz is x times z at every moment.` },
    { k: 2, label: "fit the weights", text: (q) => `<b>Step 3.</b> ${q} should be a weighted sum of the 10 terms: dX/dt ≈ Θ(X) Ξ. The weights are unknown. There are 10 for each equation, so Ξ holds 30.` },
    { k: 2, label: "fit the weights", text: (q) => `Least squares picks the weights that bring the sum closest to ${q}. None of the 30 weights is exactly 0, but most terms add almost nothing: their lines are flat.` }
  ];
  let e = 0, step = 0, tCur = 12.2, width = 0, render = () => {};
  const card = makeCard("From the data to a regression", "Press Next to add one piece at a time.");
  const { root, toolbar, body } = card;
  const mark = eyebrow(card, "The recipe");
  const st = stepper({ count: () => STEPS.length, go: (k, animate) => { step = k; render(animate); }, root, swipe: body });
  toolbar.append(st.node, st.counter, segmented(EQS, EQS[e], (v) => { e = EQS.indexOf(v); render(false); }, "Equation"));
  // Step 1: a variable on top with its tangent line, and its derivative under it
  function slopeChart(w, H) {
    const mL = 38, hAxis = 26, gap = 16;
    const hA = Math.round((H - hAxis - gap) * 0.5), yB = hA + gap, hB = H - hAxis - yB;
    const x = d3.scaleLinear().domain([t0, t1]).range([mL, w - 8]);
    const svg = d3.create("svg").attr("class", "viz-svg").attr("width", w).attr("height", H).style("touch-action", "pan-y").style("cursor", "ew-resize").attr("role", "img");
    const g = svg.append("g");
    let move = () => {};
    function set() {
      g.selectAll("*").remove();
      svg.attr("aria-label", `${VARS[e]} over 4 time units, and its slope ${EQS[e]}`);
      const v = (i) => base.X[e][i], d = (i) => base.dX[e][i];
      const yA = d3.scaleLinear().domain(d3.extent(WIN, v)).nice(4).range([hA - 6, 26]);
      const yD = d3.scaleLinear().domain(d3.extent(WIN, d)).nice(4).range([yB + hB - 6, yB + 16]);
      const axis = (y) => g.append("g").attr("class", "viz-grid").attr("transform", `translate(${mL},0)`).call(d3.axisLeft(y).ticks(3).tickSize(-(w - 8 - mL)));
      axis(yA);
      axis(yD);
      g.append("g").attr("transform", `translate(0,${H - hAxis})`).call(d3.axisBottom(x).ticks(5).tickSize(4).tickSizeOuter(0));
      g.append("text").attr("x", w - 8).attr("y", H - 1).attr("text-anchor", "end").attr("class", "viz-muted").style("font-size", "12px").text("time");
      const cursor = g.append("line").attr("y1", 4).attr("y2", H - hAxis).attr("stroke", VIZ.grey).attr("stroke-width", 1);
      const curve = (y, f) => g.append("path").attr("d", d3.line().x((i) => x(base.t[i])).y((i) => y(f(i)))(WIN)).attr("fill", "none").attr("stroke", EQC[e]).attr("stroke-width", 1.8).attr("stroke-linejoin", "round");
      curve(yA, v);
      curve(yD, d);
      // names on a halo of the page colour, so a line can pass behind them
      const name = (y, s) => g.append("text").attr("x", mL + 8).attr("y", y).attr("font-weight", 600).style("font-size", "14px")
        .attr("stroke", VIZ.bg).attr("stroke-width", 4).attr("paint-order", "stroke").text(s);
      name(14, VARS[e]);
      name(yB + 4, `${EQS[e]}: the slope of ${VARS[e]}`);
      const tangent = g.append("line").attr("stroke", VIZ.ink).attr("stroke-width", 1.8).attr("stroke-linecap", "round");
      const pA = g.append("circle").attr("r", 4).attr("fill", VIZ.ink).attr("stroke", VIZ.bg).attr("stroke-width", 2);
      const pD = g.append("circle").attr("r", 4.5).attr("fill", EQC[e]).attr("stroke", VIZ.bg).attr("stroke-width", 2);
      const value = g.append("text").style("font-size", "13px").attr("font-weight", 500).attr("stroke", VIZ.bg).attr("stroke-width", 4).attr("paint-order", "stroke");
      // one time unit and one unit of the variable, in pixels: they turn a slope into a direction on screen
      const pxT = x(t0 + 1) - x(t0), pxV = yA(1) - yA(0);
      move = () => {
        const i = Math.max(WIN[0], Math.min(WIN[WIN.length - 1], Math.round((tCur - base.t[0]) / 0.01)));
        const px = x(base.t[i]), s = d(i);
        const ux = pxT, uy = s * pxV, len = 44 / Math.hypot(ux, uy);
        cursor.attr("x1", px).attr("x2", px);
        tangent.attr("x1", px - ux * len).attr("x2", px + ux * len).attr("y1", yA(v(i)) - uy * len).attr("y2", yA(v(i)) + uy * len);
        pA.attr("cx", px).attr("cy", yA(v(i)));
        pD.attr("cx", px).attr("cy", yD(s));
        const right = px < w - 110;
        value.attr("x", px + (right ? 10 : -10)).attr("y", yD(s) + (s > 0 ? 18 : -10)).attr("text-anchor", right ? "start" : "end").text(`slope ${s < 0 ? "−" : ""}${Math.abs(s).toFixed(1)}`);
      };
      move();
    }
    // dragging moves the tangent; the drag is not passed on, so it does not also change the step
    svg.on("pointerdown pointermove", (ev) => {
      if (ev.type === "pointermove" && ev.pointerType === "mouse" && ev.buttons !== 1) return;
      if (ev.type === "pointerdown") { ev.stopPropagation(); try { svg.node().setPointerCapture(ev.pointerId); } catch (_) {} }
      tCur = x.invert(d3.pointer(ev, svg.node())[0]);
      move();
    });
    return { node: svg.node(), set };
  }
  function draw() {
    const { chart, side, cw } = split(body, width);
    side.setAttribute("aria-live", "polite");
    const rows = termRows(cw);
    const slope = slopeChart(cw, rows.height);
    const dotsNote = html`<div class="viz-note">The dots are Ξ, one column per equation: a ring is an unknown weight, a coloured dot is a weight that is not 0.</div>`;
    chart.append(slope.node, rows.node, dotsNote);
    render = (animate) => {
      const s = STEPS[step];
      mark.set(s.k, s.label);
      side.innerHTML = s.text(EQS[e], VARS[e]);
      slope.node.style.display = step === 0 ? "" : "none";
      rows.node.style.display = step === 0 ? "none" : "";
      dotsNote.style.display = step >= 2 ? "" : "none";
      if (step === 0) return slope.set();
      const all = (v) => [0, 1, 2].map(() => lib.labels.map(() => v));
      if (step === 1) rows.set({ e, mode: "library" }, animate);
      else if (step === 2) rows.set({ e, mode: "unknown", xi: all("u") }, animate);
      else rows.set({ e, mode: "fit", coef: lib.lsCoef[e], xi: all("on"), err: lib.ladders[e][0].relErr }, animate);
    };
    render(false);
  }
  watchWidth(root, (w) => { width = w; draw(); }, invalidation);
  st.refresh();
  return root;
}
```
:::

Plain least squares gives 30 non-zero weights, but the true system has only 7 terms. The two methods differ in how they decide which weights should be zero.

## Method 1: SINDy

SINDy (sparse identification of nonlinear dynamics; Brunton, Proctor and Kutz 2016) is built on the assumption that most weights in $\Xi$ are exactly zero. It estimates $\Xi$ with sequentially thresholded least squares:

1. Fit all the terms by least squares.
2. Set every weight with an absolute value below a threshold $\lambda$ to zero.
3. Refit with the terms that are left, and repeat until no weight is below $\lambda$.

As in the talk, the derivatives come from a Savitzky-Golay filter (Savitzky and Golay 1964), and $\lambda = 0.1$ as in her code.

::: {.viz-wide}
```{ojs}
viewof sindyLambda = {
  // the slider steps through round values of λ, from 0.001 to 20
  const LAMS = [0.001, 0.002, 0.005, 0.01, 0.02, 0.05, 0.1, 0.2, 0.5, 1, 2, 5, 10, 20];
  let lambda = 0.1, width = 0, render = () => {};
  // one step per pass of least squares, equation by equation, as in the slides
  let seq = [], finals = [];
  function build() {
    finals = lib.sys.eqs.map((q) => stlsq(lib.sys.G, q.b, q.yy, lambda));
    seq = [];
    finals.forEach((r, e) => r.history.forEach((h, p) => seq.push({ e, p, n: r.history.length, h, prev: p > 0 ? r.history[p - 1] : null })));
  }
  build();
  const card = makeCard(
    "Keep only the large weights",
    "Each step is one pass of least squares. A weight smaller than λ is outlined, and the next pass sets it to 0."
  );
  const { root, toolbar, body } = card;
  root.value = lambda;
  eyebrow(card, "SINDy").set(2, "fit the weights");
  const st = stepper({
    count: () => seq.length,
    go: (k, animate) => render(k, animate),
    label: (k) => `${EQS[seq[k].e]}, pass ${seq[k].p + 1} of ${seq[k].n}`,
    root, swipe: body
  });
  const slider = html`<input type="range" class="viz-range" min="0" max="${LAMS.length - 1}" step="1" aria-label="Threshold λ">`;
  slider.value = LAMS.indexOf(lambda);
  slider.setAttribute("aria-valuetext", `λ = ${fmtLambda(lambda)}`);
  const lamOut = html`<span class="viz-readout"></span>`;
  slider.addEventListener("input", () => {
    const l = LAMS[+slider.value];
    if (l === lambda) return;
    lambda = l;
    slider.setAttribute("aria-valuetext", `λ = ${fmtLambda(lambda)}`);
    build();
    // show the end result for the new λ; Back walks through its passes
    st.to(seq.length - 1, false);
  });
  // the simulation figure below follows λ when the slider is let go, not on every move
  slider.addEventListener("change", () => {
    if (root.value === lambda) return;
    root.value = lambda;
    root.dispatchEvent(new Event("input", { bubbles: true }));
  });
  toolbar.append(st.node, st.counter, html`<div class="viz-field"><span class="viz-field-label">Threshold λ</span>${slider}${lamOut}</div>`);
  function verdict() {
    const nTerms = d3.sum(finals, (r) => r.active.length);
    if (finals.every((r, j) => sameTerms(r.coef, lib.truth[j]))) return `✓ ${nTerms} terms, exactly the true ones.`;
    const lost = finals.some((r, j) => Array.from(lib.truth[j]).some((c, i) => c !== 0 && r.coef[i] === 0));
    return lost ? `✗ ${nTerms} terms. True terms are lost, so λ is too large.` : `✗ ${nTerms} terms. Extra terms stay, so λ is too small.`;
  }
  function draw() {
    const { chart, side, cw } = split(body, width);
    const rows = termRows(cw);
    chart.append(rows.node, html`<div class="viz-note">The dots are Ξ, one column per equation: a coloured dot is a weight that is kept, a small grey dot is a weight set to 0.</div>`);
    const explain = html`<div class="viz-explain" aria-live="polite"></div>`;
    const found = html`<div></div>`;
    const status = html`<div class="viz-note" style="color:var(--viz-ink);min-height:1.5em"></div>`;
    side.append(explain, html`<div class="viz-side-title">Equations found with λ = <span></span></div>`, found, status);
    const lamTitle = side.querySelector(".viz-side-title span");
    render = (pos, animate) => {
      const s = seq[pos], h = s.h, q = EQS[s.e], nA = h.active.length, last = s.p === s.n - 1;
      const active = new Set(h.active);
      lamOut.textContent = lamTitle.textContent = fmtLambda(lambda);
      // Ξ: the equations done so far as found, this one as in this pass, the others as least squares left them
      const xi = [0, 1, 2].map((j) => lib.labels.map((_, i) => (j < s.e ? finals[j].coef[i] !== 0 : j > s.e ? true : active.has(i)) ? "on" : "off"));
      const eq = lib.sys.eqs[s.e];
      rows.set({
        e: s.e, mode: "fit", coef: h.coef, xi,
        off: d3.range(lib.labels.length).filter((i) => !active.has(i)),
        below: h.below,
        err: Math.sqrt(rss(lib.sys.G, eq.b, eq.yy, h.coef) / eq.yy)
      }, animate);
      // what this pass does, in words
      const names = (ix) => ix.map((i) => termName(i)).join(", ");
      let t;
      if (nA === 0) {
        t = `<b>${q}, pass ${s.p + 1}.</b> Every weight fell below λ, so no term is left.`;
      } else {
        t = s.p === 0
          ? `<b>${q}, pass 1.</b> Least squares with all ${nA} terms.`
          : `<b>${q}, pass ${s.p + 1}.</b> The outlined weights are now 0. Least squares again with the ${nA} ${nA === 1 ? "term" : "terms"} left.`;
        const fell = s.prev ? h.below.filter((i) => Math.abs(s.prev.coef[i]) >= lambda) : [];
        if (fell.length) t += ` Refitting changes the weights: ${termName(fell[0])} is now ${fmtW(h.coef[fell[0]])}.`;
        t += h.below.length
          ? ` ${h.below.length === 1 ? "One weight is" : `${h.below.length} weights are`} smaller than λ: ${names(h.below)}.`
          : ` No weight is smaller than λ, so ${q} is done.`;
      }
      explain.innerHTML = t;
      const done = (j) => j < s.e || (j === s.e && last);
      found.innerHTML = "";
      EQS.forEach((_, j) => found.append(eqLine(j, done(j) ? finals[j].coef : null, { fixed: 2, cut: 0.005 })));
      status.textContent = pos === seq.length - 1 ? verdict() : "";
    };
  }
  watchWidth(root, (w) => { width = w; draw(); st.to(st.k, false); }, invalidation);
  return root;
}
```
:::

The figures keep the constant term, as her slides do. That is why $dz/dt$ needs one more pass than the other two equations: its constant only falls below $\lambda$ after the first refit. Move the $\lambda$ slider to see the trade-off: with a small $\lambda$, extra terms stay in, and with a large $\lambda$, true terms drop out.

::: {.viz-wide}
```{ojs}
{
  const lambda = sindyLambda;
  const coefs = lib.sys.eqs.map((q) => stlsq(lib.sys.G, q.b, q.yy, lambda).coef);
  const T = 30, h = 0.01, nT = Math.round(T / h) + 1;
  const run = simulatePoly(lib.terms, coefs, base.X.map((v) => v[0]), { h, tEnd: T });
  const outcome = runCandidate(lib.terms, coefs, base.X, { h: 0.02, tEnd: 100, keep: 10 }).outcome;
  const good = outcome === OUTCOMES[0];
  const off = base.offset;
  const dataAt = (j, i) => lorenz.X[j][i + off];
  const nModel = Math.min(nT, run.nValid);
  // the first moment when the two runs are more than 2 apart in x
  let iApart = -1;
  for (let i = 0; i < nModel; i++) if (Math.abs(run.X[0][i] - dataAt(0, i)) > 2) { iApart = i; break; }
  let tNow = T, frame = null, draw = () => {};
  const card = makeCard(
    "Simulate the model that SINDy found",
    `The equations found with λ = ${fmtLambda(lambda)}, run from the first data point. Press Play to follow the model and the data together.`
  );
  const { root, toolbar, body } = card;
  eyebrow(card, "SINDy").set(3, "simulate");
  const slider = html`<input type="range" class="viz-range" min="0" max="${T}" step="0.01" aria-label="Time">`;
  slider.value = tNow;
  const readout = html`<span class="viz-readout"></span>`;
  const stop = () => {
    if (frame) cancelAnimationFrame(frame);
    frame = null;
    play.textContent = "▶ Play";
  };
  const play = button("▶ Play", () => {
    if (frame) return stop();
    if (tNow >= T - 0.01) tNow = 0;
    play.textContent = "❚❚ Pause";
    const tick = () => {
      tNow = Math.min(T, tNow + 0.04);
      slider.value = tNow;
      draw();
      if (tNow < T) frame = requestAnimationFrame(tick);
      else stop();
    };
    frame = requestAnimationFrame(tick);
  });
  slider.oninput = () => {
    stop();
    tNow = +slider.value;
    draw();
  };
  toolbar.append(play, slider, readout, legend([["data", VIZ.grey], ["SINDy model", VIZ.ink]]));
  invalidation.then(stop);
  // a path that can be shown up to any of its points without being rebuilt: the length of the
  // line up to each point is worked out once, and the dash pattern hides the rest
  const reveal = (sel, pts) => {
    const cum = new Float64Array(pts.length);
    for (let i = 1; i < pts.length; i++) cum[i] = cum[i - 1] + Math.hypot(pts[i][0] - pts[i - 1][0], pts[i][1] - pts[i - 1][1]);
    const total = cum[pts.length - 1] + 10;
    sel.attr("d", d3.line()(pts));
    return (k) => sel.attr("stroke-dasharray", `${cum[Math.max(0, Math.min(pts.length - 1, k))]} ${total}`);
  };
  watchWidth(root, (w) => {
    body.innerHTML = "";
    const wide = w >= 680;
    const wPh = wide ? Math.floor((w - 26) * 0.44) : Math.min(w, 400);
    const wR = wide ? w - 26 - wPh : w;
    const hPh = Math.round(Math.min(360, wPh * 0.86));
    // left: both runs in the plane of x and z
    const ph = d3.create("svg").attr("class", "viz-svg").attr("width", wPh).attr("height", hPh)
      .attr("role", "img").attr("aria-label", "The data and the SINDy model in the plane of x and z");
    const xp = d3.scaleLinear().domain([-22, 22]).range([30, wPh - 6]);
    const zp = d3.scaleLinear().domain([0, 50]).range([hPh - 26, 8]);
    ph.append("g").attr("transform", `translate(0,${hPh - 26})`).call(d3.axisBottom(xp).ticks(5).tickSize(4).tickSizeOuter(0));
    ph.append("g").attr("transform", "translate(30,0)").call(d3.axisLeft(zp).ticks(5).tickSize(4).tickSizeOuter(0));
    ph.append("text").attr("x", wPh - 6).attr("y", hPh - 1).attr("text-anchor", "end").attr("font-weight", 600).style("font-size", "13px").text("x");
    ph.append("text").attr("x", 36).attr("y", 14).attr("font-weight", 600).style("font-size", "13px").text("z");
    const clip = DOM.uid("clip");
    ph.append("clipPath").attr("id", clip.id).append("rect").attr("x", 30).attr("y", 0).attr("width", wPh - 36).attr("height", hPh - 26);
    const every = (m) => d3.range(0, m, 2);
    const dataPts = every(nT).map((i) => [xp(dataAt(0, i)), zp(dataAt(2, i))]);
    const modelPts = every(nModel).map((i) => [xp(run.X[0][i]), zp(run.X[2][i])]);
    const showData = reveal(ph.append("path").attr("fill", "none").attr("stroke", VIZ.grey).attr("stroke-width", 1), dataPts);
    const showModel = reveal(ph.append("path").attr("fill", "none").attr("stroke", VIZ.ink).attr("stroke-width", 1).attr("stroke-opacity", 0.85).attr("clip-path", clip), modelPts);
    const dataDot = ph.append("circle").attr("r", 4.5).attr("fill", VIZ.grey).attr("stroke", VIZ.bg).attr("stroke-width", 2);
    const modelDot = ph.append("circle").attr("r", 4.5).attr("fill", VIZ.ink).attr("stroke", VIZ.bg).attr("stroke-width", 2).attr("clip-path", clip);
    // right: the two systems, then x over time
    const right = html`<div class="viz-col viz-side" style="width:${wR}px"></div>`;
    body.append(ph.node(), right);
    if (wR >= 440) {
      // the two systems side by side, one equation per row
      const cell = (k) => html`<span style="font-variant-numeric:tabular-nums;color:var(--viz-ink)">${eqRhs(k).text}</span>`;
      const headCell = (t) => html`<span class="viz-side-title" style="margin:0">${t}</span>`;
      right.append(html`<div style="display:grid;grid-template-columns:auto auto 1fr;gap:4px 22px;align-items:baseline;margin-bottom:14px">
        <span></span>${headCell("True system")}${headCell("Found by SINDy")}
        ${EQS.map((_, j) => [eqName(j), cell(lib.truth[j]), cell(coefs[j])]).flat()}</div>`);
    } else {
      const system = (title, list) => html`<div><div class="viz-side-title">${title}</div>${list.map((k, j) => eqLine(j, k))}</div>`;
      right.append(html`<div style="margin-bottom:12px">${system("True system", lib.truth)}${system("Found by SINDy", coefs)}</div>`);
    }
    const hT = 150, mL = 30;
    const ts = d3.create("svg").attr("class", "viz-svg").attr("width", wR).attr("height", hT)
      .attr("role", "img").attr("aria-label", "x over time: the data and the SINDy model");
    const xt = d3.scaleLinear().domain([0, T]).range([mL, wR - 6]);
    const yt = d3.scaleLinear().domain([-20, 20]).range([hT - 26, 16]);
    ts.append("g").attr("class", "viz-grid").attr("transform", `translate(${mL},0)`).call(d3.axisLeft(yt).ticks(3).tickSize(-(wR - 6 - mL)));
    ts.append("g").attr("transform", `translate(0,${hT - 26})`).call(d3.axisBottom(xt).ticks(6).tickSize(4).tickSizeOuter(0));
    ts.append("text").attr("x", wR - 6).attr("y", hT - 1).attr("text-anchor", "end").attr("class", "viz-muted").style("font-size", "12px").text("time");
    ts.append("text").attr("x", mL + 6).attr("y", 10).attr("font-weight", 600).style("font-size", "13px").text("x");
    const clip2 = DOM.uid("clip");
    const shown = ts.append("clipPath").attr("id", clip2.id).append("rect").attr("x", mL).attr("y", 0).attr("height", hT - 26);
    const series = (f, m, colour, width) => ts.append("path").attr("d", d3.line().x((i) => xt(i * h)).y((i) => yt(Math.max(-30, Math.min(30, f(i)))))(every(m)))
      .attr("fill", "none").attr("stroke", colour).attr("stroke-width", width).attr("stroke-linejoin", "round").attr("clip-path", clip2);
    series((i) => dataAt(0, i), nT, VIZ.grey, 1.2);
    series((i) => run.X[0][i], nModel, VIZ.ink, 1.2);
    if (good && iApart > 0) {
      // where the two runs separate
      const px = xt(iApart * h);
      ts.append("line").attr("x1", px).attr("x2", px).attr("y1", 16).attr("y2", hT - 26).attr("stroke", VIZ.muted).attr("stroke-dasharray", "3,3");
      ts.append("text").attr("x", px + 6).attr("y", 10).attr("class", "viz-muted").style("font-size", "12px").text(`apart from time ${(iApart * h).toFixed(1)}`);
    }
    const tCursor = ts.append("line").attr("y1", 16).attr("y2", hT - 26).attr("stroke", VIZ.ink).attr("stroke-width", 1);
    right.append(ts.node());
    const note = good
      ? "The model follows the data for a while, then the two runs separate: the system is chaotic, so a tiny difference in the weights grows. The two shapes in the plane still match."
      : `This model does not reproduce the data: its run ${outcome === OUTCOMES[4] ? "leaves the data range" : outcome === OUTCOMES[3] ? "settles to a point" : "ends up elsewhere"}. With this λ, the equations are not the true ones.`;
    right.append(html`<div class="viz-note">${note}</div>`);
    draw = () => {
      const k = Math.min(nT - 1, Math.round(tNow / h));
      const km = Math.min(k, nModel - 1);
      showData(k >> 1);
      showModel(km >> 1);
      dataDot.attr("cx", xp(dataAt(0, k))).attr("cy", zp(dataAt(2, k)));
      modelDot.attr("cx", xp(run.X[0][km])).attr("cy", zp(run.X[2][km]));
      shown.attr("width", Math.max(0, xt(tNow) - mL));
      tCursor.attr("x1", xt(tNow)).attr("x2", xt(tNow));
      readout.textContent = `time ${tNow.toFixed(1)}`;
    };
    draw();
  }, invalidation);
  return root;
}
```
:::

With $\lambda = 0.1$, the model follows the data for about 7 time units and then drifts away. That is expected for a chaotic system, even with almost exact weights, so I compare the shape of the attractor instead.

## Method 2: global modelling

Global modelling (Gouesbet and Letellier 1994) starts from the same regression, and the R package GPoM implements it (Mangiarotti et al. 2012; Mangiarotti and Huc 2019). The slides list three differences from SINDy:

- It was designed for chaotic systems: GPoM simulates each candidate and checks whether its long-term behaviour (the attractor) matches the data.
- It uses only polynomials, on the assumption that they can approximate the true system. You choose the degree (here 2, which gives the same 10 terms).
- It has no threshold. GPoM fits the weights with the Gram-Schmidt process (a way to solve least squares). Then, in each equation, it removes the term whose removal increases the error the least, refits, and repeats, keeping every model along the way.

::: {.viz-wide}
```{ojs}
{
  let e = 1, width = 0, render = () => {};
  const card = makeCard(
    "Remove one term at a time",
    "At each step the outlined term goes: its removal raises the fit error the least. Every model on the way is kept."
  );
  const { root, toolbar, body } = card;
  eyebrow(card, "Global modelling").set(2, "prune each equation");
  const L = () => gp.ladders[e];
  const plural = (k) => `${k} ${k === 1 ? "term" : "terms"}`;
  const st = stepper({
    count: () => L().length,
    go: (k, animate) => render(k, animate),
    label: (k) => `model with ${plural(L()[k].active.length)}`,
    root, swipe: body
  });
  toolbar.append(
    st.node, st.counter,
    segmented(EQS, EQS[e], (v) => { e = EQS.indexOf(v); draw(); st.to(0, false); }, "Equation")
  );
  function draw() {
    const { chart, side, cw, sw } = split(body, width, 300);
    const lad = L(), n = lib.labels.length;
    const truth = Array.from(lib.truth[e], (c) => c !== 0);
    const rows = termRows(cw, { dots: false });
    chart.append(rows.node);
    const explain = html`<div class="viz-explain" aria-live="polite"></div>`;
    // fit error against the number of terms: flat, then a jump when a true term goes
    const W = Math.min(sw, 420), H = 200, mL = 46, mB = 40;
    const x = d3.scalePoint().domain(lad.map((m) => m.active.length)).range([mL + 10, W - 14]);
    const y = d3.scaleLog().domain([1e-4, 1]).range([H - mB, 14]).clamp(true);
    const svg = d3.create("svg").attr("class", "viz-svg").attr("width", W).attr("height", H).attr("role", "img")
      .attr("aria-label", `Fit error of the 10 models of ${EQS[e]}, from 10 terms to 1`);
    for (const v of [1e-3, 1e-2, 1e-1, 1]) {
      svg.append("line").attr("x1", mL).attr("x2", W - 4).attr("y1", y(v)).attr("y2", y(v)).attr("stroke", VIZ.rule);
      svg.append("text").attr("x", mL - 6).attr("y", y(v)).attr("dy", "0.35em").attr("text-anchor", "end").attr("class", "viz-muted").style("font-size", "11.5px").text(`${100 * v}%`);
    }
    lad.forEach((m) => svg.append("text").attr("x", x(m.active.length)).attr("y", H - mB + 16).attr("text-anchor", "middle").attr("class", "viz-muted").style("font-size", "11.5px").text(m.active.length));
    svg.append("text").attr("x", (mL + W) / 2).attr("y", H - 4).attr("text-anchor", "middle").attr("class", "viz-muted").style("font-size", "12px").text("terms in the model");
    svg.append("path").attr("d", d3.line().x((m) => x(m.active.length)).y((m) => y(m.relErr))(lad)).attr("fill", "none").attr("stroke", EQC[e]).attr("stroke-width", 1.5);
    const pts = svg.append("g").selectAll("circle").data(lad).join("circle").attr("cx", (m) => x(m.active.length)).attr("cy", (m) => y(m.relErr));
    const value = svg.append("text").attr("font-weight", 500).style("font-size", "13px").attr("stroke", VIZ.bg).attr("stroke-width", 4).attr("paint-order", "stroke");
    // a tap on a model's column goes to that model
    const band = x.step();
    svg.append("g").selectAll("rect").data(lad).join("rect").attr("x", (m) => x(m.active.length) - band / 2).attr("y", 0).attr("width", band).attr("height", H - 22)
      .attr("fill", "transparent").style("cursor", "pointer").on("click", (ev, m) => st.to(lad.indexOf(m)));
    const model = html`<div style="margin-top:6px"></div>`;
    side.append(explain, html`<div class="viz-side-title">Fit error of each model (log scale)</div>`, svg.node(), model);
    render = (k, animate) => {
      const m = lad[k], active = new Set(m.active);
      rows.set({
        e, mode: "fit", coef: m.coef, err: m.relErr,
        off: d3.range(n).filter((i) => !active.has(i)),
        below: m.next === null ? [] : [m.next]
      }, animate);
      pts.attr("r", (d) => (d === m ? 5.5 : 3.5)).attr("fill", (d) => (d === m ? EQC[e] : VIZ.bg)).attr("stroke", EQC[e]).attr("stroke-width", 1.5);
      // the error can only rise to the right, so the label sits up and to the left of its point
      const px = x(m.active.length), right = k < 2;
      value.attr("x", px + (right ? -4 : 4)).attr("y", y(m.relErr) - 11).attr("text-anchor", right ? "start" : "end").text(fmtPct(m.relErr));
      const exact = m.active.length === truth.filter(Boolean).length && m.active.every((i) => truth[i]);
      const prev = k > 0 ? lad[k - 1] : null;
      let t = `<b>${plural(m.active.length)}.</b> `;
      if (prev && m.relErr > 3 * prev.relErr) t += `Without ${termName(prev.next)}, the sum no longer follows ${EQS[e]}: the fit error rises to ${fmtPct(m.relErr)}. `;
      else if (exact) t += `These are exactly the true terms, and the fit is as good as with all 10. `;
      else if (k === 0) t += `Least squares with all the terms. `;
      t += m.next === null
        ? `One term is left, so the sequence ends. GPoM keeps all ${lad.length} models.`
        : `Next to go: ${termName(m.next)}.${truth[m.next] ? " It is a true term." : ""}`;
      explain.innerHTML = t;
      model.innerHTML = "";
      model.append(eqLine(e, m.coef, { cut: 0.005, fixed: 2 }));
    };
  }
  watchWidth(root, (w) => { width = w; draw(); st.to(st.k, false); }, invalidation);
  return root;
}
```
:::

Each equation now has a sequence of 10 nested models, from 10 terms down to 1. GPoM builds candidate systems by taking one model from each sequence, within a range of total terms that you set. For example, 6 terms can be split across the three equations in 10 ways, such as (2, 2, 2), (1, 3, 2) or (4, 1, 1). Her code allows 6 to 11 terms, which gives 155 candidates.

::: {.viz-wide}
```{ojs}
{
  const TOTALS = d3.range(6, 12);
  const byTotal = new Map(TOTALS.map((t) => [t, gp.models.filter((m) => m.nTerms === t)]));
  const data = thin(base.t.length, 900).map((i) => [base.X[0][i], base.X[2][i]]);
  const GOOD = OUTCOMES[0];
  let total = 6, pick = null, width = 0, job = 0, draw = () => {};
  const card = makeCard(
    "Combine one model per equation, then simulate",
    "Each candidate takes one model from each equation's sequence. All are simulated for 100 time units, and ✓ marks the ones that reproduce the attractor. Pick a candidate to see its equations."
  );
  const { root, toolbar, body } = card;
  eyebrow(card, "Global modelling").set(3, "combine and simulate");
  const summary = html`<span class="viz-readout" aria-live="polite"></span>`;
  toolbar.append(segmented(TOTALS, total, (v) => { total = v; pick = null; draw(); }, "Total terms"), summary);
  invalidation.then(() => { job++; });
  // simulate a candidate the first time it is needed, and keep only what the figure draws
  function runOf(m) {
    let r = gpCache.runs.get(m.id);
    if (!r) {
      const coefs = m.steps.map((j, q) => gp.ladders[q][j].coef);
      const res = runCandidate(gp.terms, coefs, base.X, { stats: gpCache.stats, scorer: gpCache.scorer, keep: 2600 });
      const xz = new Float32Array(2 * res.path.length);
      res.path.forEach((p, i) => { xz[2 * i] = p.x; xz[2 * i + 1] = p.z; });
      r = { id: m.id, perEq: m.perEq, nTerms: m.nTerms, coefs, outcome: res.outcome, xz };
      gpCache.runs.set(m.id, r);
    }
    return r;
  }
  const pathXZ = (xz, from, n, xs, zs) => {
    let d = "";
    for (let i = from; i < n; i++) d += `${i > from ? "L" : "M"}${xs(xz[2 * i]).toFixed(1)},${zs(xz[2 * i + 1]).toFixed(1)}`;
    return d;
  };
  // how a candidate's terms are split over the equations: one small square per term, in the equation's colour
  const pips = (perEq) => html`<span style="display:inline-flex;gap:4px;vertical-align:middle" aria-hidden="true">${perEq.map((c, j) =>
    html`<span style="display:inline-flex;gap:1.5px">${d3.range(c).map(() => html`<i style="width:4px;height:4px;border-radius:1px;background:${EQC[j]}"></i>`)}</span>`)}</span>`;
  draw = () => {
    const my = ++job;
    const { chart, side, cw, sw, wide } = split(body, width, 320);
    const cands = byTotal.get(total);
    const few = cands.length <= 15, some = cands.length <= 28;
    const perRow = cw >= 520 ? (few ? 4 : some ? 5 : 6) : few ? 3 : 4;
    const size = Math.floor((cw - (perRow - 1) * 6) / perRow) - 2;
    const hh = Math.round(size * 0.72);
    const xs = d3.scaleLinear().domain([-25, 25]).range([4, size - 4]);
    const zs = d3.scaleLinear().domain([-2, 52]).range([hh - 6, 16]);
    const dataPath = d3.line().x((d) => xs(d[0])).y((d) => zs(d[1]))(data);
    const grid = html`<div class="viz-thumbs" style="grid-template-columns:repeat(${perRow}, ${size + 2}px)"></div>`;
    chart.append(grid);
    const thumbs = cands.map((m) => {
      const svg = d3.create("svg").attr("class", "viz-svg").attr("width", size).attr("height", hh).style("overflow", "hidden");
      svg.append("path").attr("d", dataPath).attr("class", "viz-faint").attr("stroke-width", 0.8);
      const model = svg.append("path").attr("fill", "none").attr("stroke-linejoin", "round");
      const end = svg.append("circle").attr("r", 0);
      const tick = svg.append("text").attr("x", size - 7).attr("y", 14).attr("text-anchor", "end").attr("font-weight", 600).style("font-size", "13px");
      const el = html`<button type="button" class="viz-thumb" aria-label="Model ${m.id}">${svg.node()}<span class="viz-tag">${m.id}</span>
        <span style="display:flex;justify-content:center;padding:1px 0 7px;line-height:0">${pips(m.perEq)}</span></button>`;
      el.onclick = () => {
        if (!gpCache.runs.has(m.id)) return;
        pick = m.id;
        thumbs.forEach((t) => t.el.classList.toggle("on", t.m.id === pick));
        showDetail(true);
      };
      grid.append(el);
      // the run, once it is ready: ink when it reproduces the attractor, grey when it does not
      const fill = (r) => {
        const good = r.outcome === GOOD, n = r.xz.length / 2;
        model.attr("d", n > 1 ? pathXZ(r.xz, good ? Math.round(0.7 * n) : 0, n, xs, zs) : null).attr("stroke", good ? VIZ.ink : VIZ.grey).attr("stroke-width", good ? 0.7 : 1).attr("stroke-opacity", good ? 0.7 : 1);
        if (r.outcome === OUTCOMES[3] && n) end.attr("cx", xs(r.xz[2 * n - 2])).attr("cy", zs(r.xz[2 * n - 1])).attr("r", 3).attr("fill", VIZ.grey).attr("stroke", VIZ.bg).attr("stroke-width", 1.5);
        tick.text(good ? "✓" : "");
        el.setAttribute("aria-label", `Model ${m.id}, ${m.perEq.join(" + ")} terms: ${r.outcome}`);
        el.title = `Model ${m.id}: ${r.outcome}`;
      };
      return { m, el, fill };
    });
    // the chosen candidate
    const head = html`<div style="font-weight:600;color:var(--viz-ink)"></div>`;
    const verdict = html`<div style="margin:2px 0 8px"></div>`;
    const eqs = html`<div></div>`;
    const cmp = html`<div class="viz-note"></div>`;
    const plot = html`<div style="margin-top:10px"></div>`;
    side.append(head, verdict, eqs, cmp, plot);
    function showDetail(byTap) {
      const c = gpCache.runs.get(pick);
      if (!c) return;
      const good = c.outcome === GOOD;
      head.innerHTML = "";
      head.append(`Model ${c.id}: ${c.perEq.join(" + ")} = ${c.nTerms} terms `, pips(c.perEq));
      verdict.textContent = `${good ? "✓" : "✗"} ${c.outcome}`;
      eqs.innerHTML = "";
      c.coefs.forEach((k, j) => eqs.append(eqLine(j, k, { cut: 0.01, digits: 3 })));
      const notes = [];
      [0, 1, 2].forEach((j) => {
        const k = c.coefs[j];
        const missing = lib.labels.filter((_, i) => lib.truth[j][i] !== 0 && k[i] === 0);
        const extra = lib.labels.filter((_, i) => lib.truth[j][i] === 0 && k[i] !== 0);
        if (missing.length) notes.push(`${EQS[j]} has no ${missing.join(" or ")} term`);
        if (extra.length) notes.push(`${EQS[j]} has the extra ${extra.length === 1 ? "term" : "terms"} ${extra.join(", ")}`);
      });
      cmp.textContent = notes.length ? `Compared with the true system: ${notes.join("; ")}.` : "These are exactly the terms of the true system.";
      // its run again, with every point, for the large picture
      const run = simulatePoly(gp.terms, c.coefs, base.X.map((v) => v[0]), { h: 0.02, tEnd: 100 });
      const pw = Math.min(sw, 400), phh = Math.round(pw * 0.74);
      const svg = d3.create("svg").attr("class", "viz-svg").attr("width", pw).attr("height", phh)
        .attr("role", "img").attr("aria-label", `Model ${c.id} and the data in the plane of x and z`);
      const xp = d3.scaleLinear().domain([-25, 25]).range([30, pw - 6]);
      const zp = d3.scaleLinear().domain([-2, 52]).range([phh - 26, 6]);
      svg.append("g").attr("transform", `translate(0,${phh - 26})`).call(d3.axisBottom(xp).ticks(5).tickSize(4).tickSizeOuter(0));
      svg.append("g").attr("transform", "translate(30,0)").call(d3.axisLeft(zp).ticks(5).tickSize(4).tickSizeOuter(0));
      svg.append("text").attr("x", pw - 6).attr("y", phh - 1).attr("text-anchor", "end").attr("font-weight", 600).style("font-size", "13px").text("x");
      svg.append("text").attr("x", 36).attr("y", 14).attr("font-weight", 600).style("font-size", "13px").text("z");
      const clip = DOM.uid("clip");
      svg.append("clipPath").attr("id", clip.id).append("rect").attr("x", 30).attr("y", 0).attr("width", pw - 36).attr("height", phh - 26);
      svg.append("path").attr("d", d3.line().x((d) => xp(d[0])).y((d) => zp(d[1]))(data)).attr("class", "viz-faint");
      const nV = run.nValid;
      // a run that works is drawn over its last 40 time units, so the picture stays light
      const path = svg.append("path").attr("d", nV > 1 ? d3.line().x((i) => xp(run.X[0][i])).y((i) => zp(run.X[2][i]))(d3.range(good ? Math.round(0.6 * nV) : 0, nV)) : null).attr("fill", "none")
        .attr("stroke", good ? VIZ.ink : VIZ.grey).attr("stroke-width", good ? 0.8 : 1).attr("stroke-opacity", good ? 0.7 : 1).attr("stroke-linejoin", "round").attr("clip-path", clip);
      if (c.outcome === OUTCOMES[3] && nV) {
        svg.append("circle").attr("cx", xp(run.X[0][nV - 1])).attr("cy", zp(run.X[2][nV - 1])).attr("r", 4.5).attr("fill", VIZ.grey).attr("stroke", VIZ.bg).attr("stroke-width", 2);
      }
      plot.innerHTML = "";
      plot.append(svg.node(), legend([["data", VIZ.faint], [`model ${c.id}`, good ? VIZ.ink : VIZ.grey]]));
      if (byTap && motion(1) > 0 && nV > 1) {
        const len = path.node().getTotalLength();
        path.attr("stroke-dasharray", `${len} ${len}`).attr("stroke-dashoffset", len)
          .transition().duration(motion(1400)).ease(d3.easeLinear).attr("stroke-dashoffset", 0)
          .on("end", () => path.attr("stroke-dasharray", null));
      }
      // on a narrow card the details sit under the grid: bring them into view after a tap
      if (byTap && !wide) {
        const box = side.getBoundingClientRect();
        if (box.top > innerHeight - 120) side.scrollIntoView({ block: "start", behavior: motion(1) > 0 ? "smooth" : "auto" });
      }
    }
    // simulate in slices of about 10 ms, so scrolling and tapping stay smooth
    const queue = thumbs.slice();
    const tick = () => {
      if (my !== job) return;
      const t0 = performance.now();
      while (queue.length && performance.now() - t0 < 10) {
        const t = queue.shift();
        t.fill(runOf(t.m));
      }
      const ready = cands.filter((m) => gpCache.runs.has(m.id)).map((m) => gpCache.runs.get(m.id));
      const nGood = ready.filter((r) => r.outcome === GOOD).length;
      summary.textContent = queue.length
        ? `simulating ${ready.length} of ${cands.length}`
        : `✓ ${nGood} of ${cands.length} reproduce the attractor`;
      if (queue.length) {
        setTimeout(tick, 0);
      } else {
        if (pick === null || !cands.some((m) => m.id === pick)) pick = (ready.find((r) => r.outcome === GOOD) || ready[0]).id;
        thumbs.forEach((t) => t.el.classList.toggle("on", t.m.id === pick));
        showDetail(false);
      }
    };
    tick();
  };
  watchWidth(root, (w) => { width = w; draw(); }, invalidation);
  return root;
}
```
:::

GPoM labels each candidate as diverging, periodic or unclassified, and leaves the final choice to you (the ✓ in the figure follows my own simpler rule). Her slides show nine candidates that reproduce the attractor. Model 18 has exactly the true terms. Model 5 also works with only 6 terms, but its $dy/dt$ has no $y$ term. The pruning figure shows why: $y$ adds little to $dy/dt$, so removing it raises the fit error only to about 4%.

## SINDy and global modelling side by side

|  | SINDy | Global modelling (GPoM) |
|---|---|---|
| How terms leave | Every weight smaller than $\lambda$ in absolute value is set to zero, then the model is refitted | One term at a time: the one whose removal increases the error the least |
| What comes out | One sparse model | A sequence of models per equation, combined into many candidate systems |
| How a model is judged | By its fit to the derivatives, with simulation as an extra check | By simulation: does it reproduce the attractor? |
| What you choose | $\lambda$ | The polynomial degree, the range of total terms, and the final model |

## What is still hard

The Lorenz data here are clean and complete. Real data rarely are, and the slides list three problems:

- Measurement noise makes the derivatives in step 1 unreliable. Smoothing the data first (for example with splines) can help, and so can weak or integral forms of SINDy, which integrate over time instead of differentiating the data (Schaeffer and McCalla 2017; Messenger and Bortz 2021).
- Often only some variables are measured. The dynamics can sometimes be rebuilt from time-delayed copies (Takens 1981) or derivatives (Gouesbet and Letellier 1994) of one measured variable. Her notes add that this depends on how that variable is coupled to the unmeasured ones.
- It is not always clear which measured variables belong in the model.

## Where it could help

Quynh Anh suggested three possible uses in our field:

- It could show how pathogens that circulate in the same population interact, or that they do not.
- It could model how physiological signals change and detect when their dynamics shift.
- It could infer unobserved states, such as the dynamics of vectors in vector-borne diseases.

Some studies have already tried this on epidemic data: SINDy on case reports of measles, chickenpox and rubella (Horrocks and Bauch 2020), and global modelling on the early COVID-19 epidemics (Mangiarotti et al. 2020).

## Key things to remember

- Equation discovery does not replace mechanistic models. A discovered equation is a hypothesis that needs validation and interpretation.
- A regression method can only choose from the library you give it. If a true term is missing, no threshold can add it.
- Several models can reproduce the same data, like models 5 and 18 here, so choosing among them needs other reasons: fewer terms, prediction tests, or knowledge of the system.
- For a chaotic system, compare attractors, not exact paths.

To try these methods yourself, use PySINDy, a Python package for SINDy (de Silva et al. 2020), or GPoM, an R package for global modelling.

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" icon=false}
## R code (shortened from the talk)

The SINDy part (steps 1 to 3) was checked in R with a simple stand-in for `drvSucc()`, and it returns the exact Lorenz coefficients. The GPoM calls have not been run here; they use the same functions and settings as the talk's code.

```r
library(tidyverse)
library(deSolve)
library(GPoM)

# Simulate the Lorenz system (the talk used odin2 and dust2)
lorenz <- function(t, s, p) {
  with(as.list(c(s, p)), list(c(
    sigma * (y - x),
    x * (rho - z) - y,
    x * y - beta * z
  )))
}
lrz <- ode(
  y = c(x = 10, y = 10, z = 10), times = seq(0, 100, by = 0.001),
  func = lorenz, parms = c(sigma = 10, rho = 28, beta = 8 / 3)
) |>
  as.data.frame() |>
  rename(t = time)

# Step 1: derivatives with a Savitzky-Golay filter
deriv <- c("x", "y", "z") |>
  set_names() |>
  map(\(v) drvSucc(lrz$t, lrz[[v]], nDeriv = 1))
dxdt <- map(deriv, \(d) d$seriesDeriv[, 2])  # column 2 is the first derivative
t_keep <- deriv$x$tout                       # the filter drops points at each end

# Step 2: library of candidate terms (degree 2, with the constant as in the slides;
# the talk's SINDy code leaves the constant out and finds the same model)
theta <- lrz |>
  filter(t %in% t_keep) |>
  transmute(const = 1, x, y, z,
            x2 = x^2, xy = x * y, xz = x * z,
            y2 = y^2, yz = y * z, z2 = z^2)

# Step 3: sequentially thresholded least squares
stlsq <- function(theta, dxdt, lambda = 0.1, max_iter = 100) {
  theta <- as.matrix(theta)
  coefs <- rep(1, ncol(theta))  # start with every term active
  for (i in seq_len(max_iter)) {
    active <- which(coefs != 0)
    if (length(active) == 0) break
    fit <- qr.solve(theta[, active, drop = FALSE], dxdt)
    small <- abs(fit) < lambda
    coefs[active] <- if_else(small, 0, fit)
    if (!any(small)) break
  }
  set_names(coefs, colnames(theta))
}
sindy_coefs <- map(dxdt, \(d) stlsq(theta, d, lambda = 0.1))

# Step 4: simulate with GPoM::numicano().
# GPoM orders the 10 terms of a degree 2 model in 3 variables as
# 1, z, z^2, y, yz, y^2, x, xz, xy, x^2
gpom_order <- c("const", "z", "z2", "y", "yz", "y2", "x", "xz", "xy", "x2")
K <- sapply(sindy_coefs, \(k) k[gpom_order])
sim <- numicano(nVar = 3, dMax = 2, KL = K,
                onestep = 0.001, Istep = 1e5,
                v0 = c(10, 10, 10), method = "rk4")

# Global modelling with GPoM
gp <- gPoMo(as.matrix(lrz[, c("x", "y", "z")]), tin = lrz$t,
            dMax = 2, nS = c(1, 1, 1),
            nPmin = 6, nPmax = 11,
            IstepMin = 500, IstepMax = 5000,
            show = 0, verbose = FALSE)
table(gp$okMod)  # 0 = diverged, -1 = periodic, 1 = unclassified
visuEq(gp$models$mToTest5, nVar = 3, dMax = 2,
       substit = c("x", "y", "z"), approx = TRUE)
```

The figures use [`equation-discovery.js`](equation-discovery.js), a short JavaScript version of both methods. It follows the talk's code and the GPoM source, but the outcome labels in the last figure use my own simpler rules.
:::
